label: PLC 1x8 SC/APC connectorised cassette
notes: The connectorised form of plc-1x8-sca: the same 1:8 PLC chip shipped with SC/APC adapters on its input instead of a bare pigtail to splice. The chip figures are that row's, unchanged and from the same place: 9.03 dB ideal split (10*log10(8)) plus 1.47 dB excess = 10.5 dB without connectors, inside ITU-T G.671's insertion-loss requirement for a 1x8 branching component on a normal-reach span (WR1) of 8.2 dB min / 10.6 dB max. Both chip numbers are typical values - the excess is the difference between the observed total and the ideal split, not a figure from a vendor sheet - so a cassette you buy may sit up to 0.1 dB above this row on the chip alone. What the termination changes is what is charged at the splitter's input: the connectorised flag bills two SC/APC matings (the catalogue's own sc-apc row, 2 x 0.3 = 0.6 dB) where the spliced cassette bills one fusion splice (fusion, 0.1 dB), so the same plant reads 11.94 dB of ODN against 11.44 dB - 0.6 dB of matings minus 0.1 dB of splice = 0.5 dB more. The termination field is also what makes the splice diagram label this input 'splitter input (2 connectors)' instead of 'splitter input (1 splice)'. Why this row exists: nap-8 is the catalogue's 8-port closure, and the catalogue's only connectorised splitter row used to be 1x16 - this row is its 1x8 sibling - so a pre-terminated 8-port NAP either had to bill a splice it does not make (the spliced 1x8, 0.5 dB optimistic) or be drawn with a 1:16 cassette it would never buy - measured on the same plant, 15.24 dB against 11.94 dB, 3.30 dB of loss, 3.01 dB of which is the split ratio and 0.29 dB the larger chip's excess, that no 8-port closure needs. The trap when replacing this row: a cassette sheet that prints 'insertion loss <= 11.1 dB, SC/APC' has already counted its own connectors - compare that figure against 9.03 + 1.47 + 0.6 = 11.1 dB, and do not raise excessLossDb for them or they are charged twice. The rest of the ladder stays spliced because design.js resolves an auto-designed splitter as 'plc-1x' + ratio + '-sca', so this row is never picked by synthesis - it is for a plant drawn by hand, or for a splitter box or NAP whose cassettes arrive pre-terminated. Replace with the bought cassette's datasheet before construction.
